content.text: I checked every claim in the document against the record and found nothing to flag. All 18 claims are supported by rows of the record, and I've named those rows in the submission below.

supported.quote: In the files Code-Fix read, the new renderer's monthly spend summary (`average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, line {F1.1}) divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases it made this month, and nothing guards against that count being zero. So for any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError, and `serve_account_page` catches the error and returns a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Switching off a setting moved the shop's account pages onto newer code that likely breaks for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, because it tries to work out an average over zero purchases.
If legacy-checkout-fallback is turned off again, account pages could go back onto the new renderer and fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
Shoppers' account pages failed to load

It did not change what was done: the investigation weighed it as unverified and ranked legacy-checkout-fallback second, so that flag was reverted only after the revert of monthly-spend-feature was refuted.
Shoppers' account page requests failed: the service's own account-page error-rate warning rose from its usual level, and the error-rate alert fired.
Account page requests were raising ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py from the onset minute ({G5309.3}), and the account page handler turned each one into a failed page.

Account pages had moved from the legacy renderer to the new renderer, whose spend summary runs the line that raised. The legacy renderer's count was highest at {Gc27d.7} and the new renderer's at {Gc27d.11}.
The legacy-checkout-fallback flag was switched off at {P1.1}. Flag evaluations went from all on before the onset to mostly off in the onset minute, and then to all off.

The monthly-spend-feature flag, switched on at the same instant ({P2.1}): turning it off left the service at the incident's level, and the service came back with it still on once legacy-checkout-fallback was turned back on.

The new renderer's spend summary divides by the number of purchases the shopper made this month, and Code-Fix's reading of the source says that number is zero for an ordinary shopper who has not bought this month.
No check was seen that tested the new renderer's spend summary with an account that has past purchases but none this month before a flag could send production account pages to it.
Code-Fix's reading says the test file's own fixture calls such a shopper the ordinary case.

Switching off legacy-checkout-fallback took most flag evaluations off within the onset minute and all of them from the next minute, which sent all account page traffic to the new renderer. No staged rollout of the flag change to a small share of traffic was seen.
Two flags on the same service were changed by the same actor at the same instant, so the investigation could not tell from the record which one caused the errors.
The person's lead in the thread named the right flag before the investigation began, but the investigation ranked that flag second.
The first revert went to the wrong flag, and the right one waited until that revert was judged.
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.
